title: Requirements for the project
titleCn: 文学课作家研究项目要求讨论

paragraphs.text: You will hear two students discussing a project they have to do as part of a literature course on great books.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-five.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-five.
Hi, Joey. How are you doing? I heard you were sick.

Oh, hi, Olivia. Yeah, I had a virus last week, and I missed a whole pile of lectures, like the first one on the great books in literature, where Dr. Castle gave us all the information about the semester project.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text:
can give you copies of the handouts. I've got them right here.

00:01:36,000

That's okay. I already collected the handouts, but I'm not very clear about all the details. I know we each have to choose an individual author. I think I'm going to do Carlos Castaneda. I'm really interested in South American literature.

00:01:50,440

Have you checked he's on the list that Dr. Castle gave us? We can't just choose anyone.

00:01:55,280

Yeah, I checked. It's okay. Who did you choose?

00:01:58,640

Well, I was thinking of choosing Ernest Hemingway, but then I thought, "No, I'll do a British author, not an American one." So I chose Emily Brontë.

00:02:08,080

Okay. And first of all, it says we have to read a biography of our author.

00:02:13,980

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text:
guess it's okay if we just look up information about him on the Internet?

00:02:17,640

No, it's got to be a full-length book. I think the minimum length's two hundred and fifty pages. There's a list of biographies. Didn't you get that?

00:02:26,800

Oh, right. I didn't realize we had to stick with that. So what do we have to do when we've read the biography?

00:02:33,820

Well, then we have to choose one work by the writer. Again, it's got to be something quite long. We can't just read a short story.

00:02:41,380

But I guess a collection of short stories would be okay?

00:02:44,060

Yes, or even a collection of poems, they said. But I think most people are doing novels. I'm gonna do Wuthering Heights. I've read it before, but I really want to read it again now I've found out more about the writer.

00:02:57,320

And then the video. We have to make a short video about our author and about the book. How long has it got to be?

00:03:04,420

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text:
minute.

00:03:05,600

What? Like sixty seconds? We got to give all the important information about their life and the book we choose?

00:03:13,220

Well, you can't do everything. I wrote it down somewhere. Yes. Dr. Castle said we had to find or write a short passage that helps to explain the author's passion for writing, why they're a writer.

00:03:28,160

So we can back this up with reference to important events in the writer's life, if they're relevant. But it's up to us, really. The video is meant to portray the essence of the writer's life and the piece of writing we choose.

00:03:43,460

So when we read the biography, we have to think about what kind of person our writer is.

00:03:48,820

Yes, and the historical context, and so on. So for my writer, Emily Brontë, the biography gave a really strong impression of the place where she lived and the countryside around.

00:04:01,660

Right. I'm beginning to get the idea.

00:04:07,100

Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions twenty-six to thirty.

00:04:18,140

Now listen and answer questions twenty-six to thirty.

00:05:01,520

Uh, can I check the other requirements with you?

00:05:04,240

Sure.

00:05:05,840

The handout said after we'd read the biography, we had to read the work we'd chosen by our author and choose a passage that's typical in some way, that typifies the author's interests and style.

00:05:17,680

Yes, but at the same time, it has to relate to the biographical extract you choose. There's got to be some sort of theme linking them.

00:05:26,740

Okay, I'm with you.

00:05:28,400

And then you have to think about the video.

00:05:30,800

So are we meant to dramatize the scene we choose?

00:05:33,480

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text:
guess we could, but there's not a lot of time for that. I think it's more how we can use things like sound effects to create the atmosphere, the feeling we want.

00:05:43,200

And presumably visuals as well?

00:05:46,040

Yeah, of course. I mean, I suppose that's the whole point of making a video. But whatever we use has to be historically in keeping with the author. We can use things like digital image processing to do it all.

00:05:59,460

So we can use any computer software we want?

00:06:02,380

Sure. And it's important that we use a range, not just one software program. That's actually one of the things we're assessed on.

00:06:11,280

Okay.

00:06:12,600

Oh, and something else that's apparently really important is to keep track of the materials we use and to acknowledge them.

00:06:20,080

Including stuff we download off the Internet, presumably?

00:06:23,380

Yeah. So our video has to list all the material used with details of the source in a bibliography at the end.

00:06:30,900

Okay. And you were talking about assessment of the project. Did they give us the criteria? I couldn't find anything on the handout.

00:06:39,740

Sure. He gave us them in the lecture. Let's see. You get twenty-five percent just for getting all the components done. That's both sets of reading and the video. Then the second part is actually how successful we are at getting the essence of the work. They call that content, and that counts for fifty percent. Then the last twenty-five percent is on the video itself, the artistic and technical side.

00:07:06,980

Great. Well, that sounds a lot of work, but a whole lot better than just handing in a paper. Thanks a lot, Olivia.

00:07:14,180

You're welcome.

00:07:18,620

That is the end of part three. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to part three.
